content.title: About
content.content: Fruit topping (5039) is a blend of dried and/or fresh fruits designed to be added to desserts, yogurts, cereals, and drinks. The fruits retain their characteristic aroma, sweetness, and nutrients, providing a bright flavor and vivid color.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The mix may include pineapple, mango, kiwi, strawberry, blueberry and other exotic fruits.
Dried fruits in the topping keep most of their vitamins, especially vitamin C and carotenoids.
Fruit topping is often used in vegan and gluten‑free recipes as a natural sweetener.
Sugar content varies depending on the fruit types and processing level.
Traditionally, fruit topping is served in Asian cuisine, for example in sticky‑rice desserts.

items.title: Rich in vitamins
items.content: Fruits provide vitamin C, vitamin A, folate and other antioxidants that support immunity and skin health.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes healthy digestion and helps maintain a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Unlike nut toppings, fruit topping contains virtually no fat, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Supports gut microbiota
items.content: Prebiotic fibers in fruits encourage the growth of beneficial gut bacteria.

items.title: Natural sweetness
items.content: The natural sugars in fruits allow reduction of added sugar in recipes.

items.title: Fruit allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to specific fruits included in the topping.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: High natural sugar levels can be an issue for people with diabetes or those monitoring sugar intake.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: If fruits are not thoroughly washed, pesticide residues may remain.

items.title: Dried fruit glucose concentration
items.content: Dried fruits have a more concentrated glucose level, which can raise blood sugar quickly.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Fruit topping can be mixed into yogurt, oatmeal, smoothies, ice cream, baked goods, or used as a garnish for desserts. For extra aroma, fruits can be lightly toasted in a pan or oven.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the topping in an airtight container in a cool, dry place away from direct light. Dried fruits keep up to 6 months, fresh fruits up to 5 days in the refrigerator. Discard if mold or off‑odors appear.
